reader_summary.headline: James Davolos explains elegant equities for higher inflation at Horizon Kinetics.
reader_summary.overview: James Davolos of Horizon Kinetics discusses investing in capital-light businesses like royalties and exchanges. He argues that inflation will rise due to huge government debts and supply chain limits for power and copper. The firm focuses on scarce assets that hold value when prices go up.

key_points.text: Horizon Kinetics invests in capital-light businesses like royalties and exchanges because they generate cash without heavy physical assets.
key_points.evidence_quote: royalties are probably the most eloquent business model, essentially a revenue interest in the CAPX and OPEX of a miner of an oil and gas explorer

key_points.text: The firm believes inflation will rise to 3% to 5% because huge government debts cannot be paid with low interest rates forever.
key_points.evidence_quote: the number one limiting factor is government deficits and government debts are just so enormous today. So, six, seven percent deficits in the U.S.

key_points.text: Building power grids and finding copper for AI is extremely difficult because supply chains are outdated and resources like water and land are limited.
key_points.evidence_quote: the U.S. power grid essentially didn't grow for 20 years. And now they're saying 3% growth. This is just a monumental task to add that many gigawatts and that short of a time span.

key_points.text: Royalty companies offer high optionality because they earn revenue from others' expansion without spending much capital themselves.
key_points.evidence_quote: When you think about royalties, exchanges, land banks, brokerages, etc. Two things sticks out. So one is, while they are technically finite, they're much less finite in the sense that there's a lot of capacity that's available for free.

key_points.text: Investors should avoid forcing growth through bad deals or leverage, and instead invest wisely during market downturns.
key_points.evidence_quote: One of the biggest red flags and one of the hardest challenges I've seen is everybody recognizes that scale is almost essential in this business. But really talking to management and making sure they understand that growth has to be deliberate and you cannot grow just for the sake of growth.
